'''Sergey Grigori Badalyan''' ({{langx|hy|Սերգեյ Գրիգորի Բադալյան}}; 4 July 1947 – 24 November 1999) was an [[Armenia]]n politician who served as the first secretary of the [[Armenian Communist Party]] from 1991 to 1999. 

Badalyan was born in [[Yerevan]] in 1947. He studied engineering and mathematics at the [[National Polytechnic University of Armenia|Yerevan Polytechnic Institute]]. He worked at the institute as an assistant professor from 1970 to 1973. From 1973 to 1980, he worked at the Joint Institute of Nuclear Research in [[Dubna]]. From 1980 to 1982, he was the head of the scientific research group at the Yerevan Institute of Physics, then served as the secretary of the Communist Party committee of the same institute from 1982 to 1991.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sergey Grigori Badalyan |url=http://www.parliament.am/deputies.php?sel=details&ID=304&lang=arm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220616191620/http://www.parliament.am/deputies.php?sel=details&ID=304&lang=arm |archive-date=2022-06-16 |access-date=2023-07-31 |website=National Assembly of the Republic of Armenia}}</ref> 

Badalyan was elected to the [[National Assembly (Armenia)|National Assembly of Armenia]] as a deputy from the Armenian Communist Party in the parliamentary elections of [[1995 Armenian parliamentary election|1995]] and [[1999 Armenian parliamentary election|1999]]. He led the Communist Party's parliamentary faction and served on the parliamentary committee on foreign relations.<ref name=":0" /> Badalyan stood as the Armenian Communist Party's presidential candidate in the [[1996 Armenian presidential election|1996]] and [[1998 Armenian presidential election|1998 presidential elections]]. He came in third place in the 1996 election with 79,347 votes (6.30% of the total votes) and fourth place in the 1998 election with 155,023 votes (10.93%).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Nohlen |first=Dieter |title=Elections in Asia and the Pacific: A Data Handbook |last2=Grotz |first2=Florian |last3=Hartmann |first3=Christof |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2001 |isbn=9780191530418 |volume=I |pages=329}}</ref> 
[[File:Sergey Badalyan's plaque.JPG|thumb|Plaque dedicated to Sergey Badalyan on his former home in Yerevan]]
He was a "special guest" of the [[Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe]] from 20 September 1999 to 24 January 2000,<ref name="Council of Europe - Mr Sergey BADALYAN">{{cite web |title=Mr Sergey Badalyan |url=http://assembly.coe.int/ASP/AssemblyList/AL_MemberDetails.asp?MemberID=6239 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081107071112/https://assembly.coe.int/ASP/AssemblyList/AL_MemberDetails.asp?MemberID=6239 |archive-date=2008-11-07 |accessdate=5 May 2012 |publisher=[[Council of Europe]]}}</ref> although he died before the completion of his tenure.<ref name="Dead">{{cite news |last=Musayelyan |first=Suren |date=2006-07-14 |title=Better Red than Dead: Communist party makes efforts to regain status |publisher=ArmeniaNow.com |url=http://www.armenianow.com/hy/node/6526 |url-status=dead |accessdate=2012-05-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008051227/https://www.armenianow.com/hy/node/6526 |archive-date=2018-10-08}}</ref>

Badalyan died suddenly in Moscow  in November 1999 at the age of 52.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-10-26 |title=PS Retro: Sergey Badalyan was encouraged by Russian fighters (video) |url=https://a1plus.am/en/article/152058 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230731124308/https://a1plus.am/en/article/152058 |archive-date=2023-07-31 |access-date=2023-07-31 |website=A1Plus |language=en}}</ref> Internal divisions ensued in the Armenian Communist Party following Badalyan's death, and the party ceased to be a significant political force.<ref name="Dead" />
